identity.title: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering

problem.claim: Measure how well AI agents perform machine learning engineering.

contributions.claim: Introduces MLE-bench, built from 75 Kaggle ML engineering competitions covering tasks such as model training, dataset preparation, and experiment execution.
Establishes human baselines from publicly available Kaggle leaderboards and evaluates several frontier language models using open-source agent scaffolds.
Open-sources the benchmark code to support future research on AI agents’ ML engineering capabilities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present MLE-bench as a benchmark specifically for measuring AI-agent performance on machine learning engineering, using a diverse collection of real-world competition tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the best-performing setup, OpenAI’s o1-preview with AIDE scaffolding, reaches at least Kaggle bronze-medal level in 16.9% of competitions.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper introduces MLE-bench for measuring AI agents’ machine learning engineering performance.
It curates 75 Kaggle competitions spanning practical ML engineering activities and establishes leaderboard-based human baselines.
Open-source agent scaffolds are used to evaluate several frontier language models; the strongest reported setup reaches bronze-medal level in 16.9% of competitions.
The authors investigate resource scaling and pre-training contamination, then release the benchmark code for future research.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark combines a diverse task suite, human leaderboard baselines, and a thresholded competition outcome.

lessons.interpretation: This aligns evaluation scope, reference points, and an interpretable performance criterion.
lessons.application: For an agent benchmark, define varied real-world tasks, establish an external human reference, and report performance against a concrete threshold.
lessons.exception: This approach may be unsuitable when public leaderboard baselines or task outcomes are unavailable or incomparable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the full model set, resource-scaling findings, contamination results, or detailed evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not report whether the 16.9% result is statistically estimated, replicated, or directly comparable across competitions.
